rationale: Single replacement of the encoder stage-0 module boundary model.resnet.encoder.stages.0 (ResNetStage, group 928c554228ed389eec5f): an eager composite that micro-batches the frozen batch-32 request along the batch dimension, extending the pattern the evaluator already accepted for the stem. How previous-feedback shapes this attempt: the prior trial-e9279012c6 (stem micro-batch, bundle trial-e9279012c6-param-9ac5fd08) was ACCEPTED (decision.accepted true, quality pass, max_abs_error 0.0) and is verified executing in the current revision cd0790cf (coverage route stem_microbatch_rows8, reference invocations 8/8), so there is no rejected implementation to repair: the only candidate_diagnostics events are _training_active returning False at trial-e9279012c6.py:50, which the supplied source shows is the normal eval-mode predicate of its signature guard, not a failure. This candidate therefore keeps those exact guard/fallback semantics (training predicate, signature/contiguity/dtype checks, parent re-execution on runtime error, {} build on missing references) and applies the pattern to the tier that now binds the objective. Measured facts: the current accepted peak is 203,099,136 B (project_measurement, both AB/BA endpoints, zero noise; throughput 8079-8121 img/s vs floor 7158.9) and decomposes exactly as params 46,758,048 + input 19,267,584 + cudnn workspace 8,622,944 + 5 x 25,690,112, where 25,690,112 B is one 32x64x56x56 FP32 activation; the parameter search measured stem chunk rows 4 and 8 both at exactly 203,099,136 (stem no longer binding) while rows 16 rose to 205,196,288; per target-resources the stages.0 subtree runs out-of-place conv->batch_norm chains with out-of-place post-add ReLU around the in-place residual add, and 32x64x56x56 tensors exist only in stage 0 and its input (the stem output). Five such tensors coexist at the second BasicLayer's trailing batch_norm (stage input, layers.0 output kept as residual, layers.1 relu0 output, conv1 output, bn1 output). Every stage-0 operator (valid 3x3 conv, eval BatchNorm, ReLU, residual add) is per-sample, so the boundary chunks exactly: the replacement slices the contiguous [32,64,56,56] input into contiguous row chunks (no copies, no row skipped), runs each chunk through the unchanged BasicLayer parents stages.0.layers.0 (f3ec7e68beb5e3d3f846d2fa) and stages.0.layers.1 (dfb96bb329e6c3859d690b9a) via context.references, and assembles chunk results into one [32,64,56,56] tensor for the untouched stages 1-3; the parents' internal in-place residual add touches only tensors freshly allocated inside each parent call, never the input views (CPU replica with the real transformers modules: chunk rows 4/5/8/16/32 all bitwise equal to the parent stage forward and the input unmutated). No module.forward wrapper is installed by the candidate and no functional sites are declared, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies with no unrelated dispatch cost. Composition: the installed stem bundle writes only call d16297b8a11b79a2657853d0, this bundle writes only 595c8331c60823c132ca3a4a - no overlapping call writes, so requires/replaces stay empty and the bundles compose additively; stem, pooler, classifier and stages 1-3 run exactly as in the accepted revision. Hypotheses to be tested by the evaluator's clean measurement (not observed facts): at stage0_chunk_rows=8 the stage-0 worst moment becomes stem output 25,690,112 + assembled output 25,690,112 + 4 chunk transients x 6,422,528 = 77,070,336, so the peak should drop to the tier already set outside the region, ~151,718,912 B (-25.3%), matching the unchanged stem tier (input 19,267,584 + stem out 25,690,112 + 2 x 6,422,528 chunk transients) and stage-1 tier (stage-0 output + 4 x 12,845,056); the honest pessimistic bound is 177,409,024 B (-12.7%) because static call-shape analysis explains only 4 of the 5 coexisting activations, and a rows-16 chunk lands at exactly that 177,409,024 tier (stem out + assembled + 4 x 12,845,056). Throughput: ~0.5 ms headroom exists (accepted 3.92-3.96 ms vs 4.47 ms floor); the stem precedent measured batch-8 chunking faster than baseline and batch-4 +0.44 ms, and stage 0 adds ~54 already-warmed launches at rows 8, so images_per_second >= 7158.9 is expected to hold with stage0_chunk_rows=16 as the launch-light fallback. Numerics: identical aten kernels on contiguous batch slices with per-sample-exact BN(eval)/ReLU/add; the accepted stem bundles measured max_abs_error 0.0 at rows 4/8/16 and the CPU replica of this composition is bit-identical, so logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 are expected - only the evaluator's reference comparison decides. The four stages.1-family calls included in affected_calls (47f42cfd2d55620ecd13e733, b92e9ace8737abe290b03c62, ae6782daa6589784cea3aad8, 6d17e25a4f8679b7b8f3d445) are listed because their group families share ownership across stages.0/stages.1; their own execution is unchanged.

setup_work.build_time_gpu_work: none: build(context) only resolves context.references/context.modules for the three stage-0 call IDs, reads stage0_chunk_rows from context['parameters'] (default 8, malformed values fall back to the default, minimum 2) and returns one closure; no tensors are allocated, no parameters are transformed, no model state changes, no fixture-dependent precomputation, no CUDA-graph capture. If any of the three references is absent, build returns {} - a concise setup failure that installs nothing rather than silently routing every call to the parent.
setup_work.first_invocation_behavior: the chunked path allocates through the normal CUDA caching allocator during the framework's 2 warmup invocations, so the recurring blocks (four-to-five 6,422,528 B chunk transients at rows 8, the 25,690,112 B assembled stage-0 output, per-chunk cudnn workspaces) are already cached when the 5 timed repeats run; reset_peak_memory_stats() observes allocator reuse, not cudaMalloc storms. Every invocation recomputes from the current input through the parent callables - nothing fixture-dependent is cached.
setup_work.memory_scope: no CUDA Graph capture and no allocation migration into retained graph pools: every stage-0 allocation stays inside the measured peak_allocated_bytes counter. Expected framework.peak_allocated_bytes ~151,718,912 B at rows 8 (pessimistic 177,409,024 at rows 16 or if one unexplained 25,690,112 term persists) vs the accepted 203,099,136; framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes stays at its preparation-set 280,297,472 because model preparation already peaks above any run peak; setup adds nothing to either counter. Reserved pools may shift with the new chunk-sized blocks (stem evidence: peak_reserved moved 429,916,160 -> 459,276,288 between rows 8 and 4) - reserved memory is outside the objective and no counter decrease is claimed as a general physical-memory saving.

quality_risks: Numerics: cudnn may select a different conv algorithm at batch-8/16 chunks, reordering the 576-term accumulations and producing ulp-level logits differences; quality requires full 1000-class logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 - expected to hold comfortably (eval BatchNorm, ReLU and the residual add are value-exact under row chunking and a CPU replica of this exact composition over the real transformers ResNetBasicLayer modules is bit-identical for rows 4/5/8/16/32; the accepted stem micro-batch measured max_abs_error 0.0 at all tested chunk sizes), but only the evaluator's reference comparison against offline-reference semantics decides.

Throughput: if batch-8 kernel-efficiency loss plus the ~54 extra launches exceed the ~0.5 ms headroom over the accepted 3.92-3.96 ms (floor 4.47 ms = 7158.9 img/s), the constraint could fail; the declared stage0_chunk_rows=16 variant halves launches at a ~177,409,024 B peak and rows=4 trades launches for the same ~151.7 MB floor, so the existing TaskSearch/TPE loop can select within the boundary without changing workload semantics.

Fallback semantics: any exception inside the chunked path re-executes the whole stage through the parent reference (idempotent under eval/inference_mode; the parents' in-place add never mutated the input views, verified CPU-side) and self-reports stage0_parent_runtime_fallback:<type>; guards route unexpected args/kwargs, non-contiguous, non-float32, non-64-channel, CPU, requires-grad or training-mode calls to the parent with stage0_parent_signature_fallback, so adversarial or unseen calls preserve exact parent behavior; the diagnostics-visible False returns of the training predicate are normal eval-mode guards, as established for the accepted stem bundle.

Coverage and composition: the only replaced boundary is stages.0; layers.0/layers.1 keep executing through context.references 4x per invocation at rows 8 (CPU replica shows exactly 4/4 reference invocations and route label stage0_microbatch_rows8), so all 72 selection-listed stage-0-subtree calls (modules, aten conv2d/batch_norm/relu/add_ and the record_function hooks) keep executing with invocation counts 1->4; no calls are eliminated and no counter is filled with unused work; the stem bundle at d16297b8a11b79a2657853d0 is untouched, and the four stages.1-family calls listed through shared group families execute unchanged.

Memory accounting: if cudnn retains a different workspace for batch-8/16 stage-0 convolutions than the current 8,622,944 B, the peak moves by that delta; workspace retention and the exact 4-vs-5 activation coexistence are observable only through the evaluator's counter, which is why the 151,718,912 estimate is stated as a hypothesis with the 177,409,024 pessimistic bound.

params.name: stage0_chunk_rows
params.description: Contiguous rows per encoder stage-0 micro-batch within the frozen batch-32 request (remainder chunks handled generically; batch, workload and semantics unchanged). 8 (default) and 4 target the ~151,718,912 B tier already set by the unchanged stem and stage 1; 16 halves launch overhead at a ~177,409,024 B stage-0-limited peak.
